hadiths.text: When the month of Ramadan starts, the gates of heaven are opened and the gates of Hell are closed and the devils are chained.
hadiths.context: This hadith highlights the special spiritual atmosphere of Ramadan, emphasizing that it is a time of increased mercy and opportunity for good deeds.

hadiths.text: Whoever fasts during Ramadan out of sincere faith and hoping to attain Allah's rewards, all his past sins will be forgiven.
hadiths.context: This emphasizes that the intention behind fasting is as important as the act itself. Fasting with faith and hope brings spiritual renewal.

hadiths.text: Take suhoor as there is a blessing in it.
hadiths.context: The Prophet encouraged eating before dawn, even if just a small amount. This pre-dawn meal provides both physical energy and spiritual blessing.

hadiths.text: When one of you is fasting, he should abstain from indecent acts and unnecessary talk. If someone insults him or quarrels with him, he should say: 'I am fasting.'
hadiths.context: Fasting extends beyond food and drink—it's about self-control in all aspects, including speech and behavior.

hadiths.text: The people will remain on the right path as long as they hasten the breaking of the fast.
hadiths.context: Breaking the fast immediately at sunset is encouraged. Delaying unnecessarily is discouraged in Islamic tradition.

hadiths.text: Allah said: 'Every deed of the son of Adam is for him except fasting; it is for Me, and I shall reward for it.'
hadiths.context: This sacred hadith (Hadith Qudsi) emphasizes the unique status of fasting among acts of worship—its reward is known only to Allah.

hadiths.text: Whoever gives iftar to one who is fasting will have a reward like his, without that detracting from the reward of the fasting person in the slightest.
hadiths.context: Generosity during Ramadan is highly encouraged. Feeding others who are fasting multiplies blessings for both parties.

hadiths.text: Look for Laylat al-Qadr in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
hadiths.context: The Night of Power, better than a thousand months, falls within the last ten nights. Muslims often spend these nights in increased worship.
